_comment: Judge knowledge base. 'techniques': response guidance per MITRE ATT&CK technique (the 6 seed techniques plus T1498, T1499, T1046 to cover Detection's DoS, DDoS and PortScan categories; Heartbleed maps to T1190). 'category_techniques': which techniques are consistent with each Detection attack category (Detection tags detector_notes with [category=...]).

T1110.name: Brute Force
T1110.guidance: Repeated authentication attempts against a service. Blocking the source and locking targeted accounts is appropriate when the source is external. Escalate if the source is internal or if any login succeeded.

T1110.001.name: Brute Force: Password Guessing
T1110.001.guidance: Automated guessing of account passwords (e.g. SSH-Patator, FTP-Patator). Lock the targeted accounts and block the source. Escalate if a login succeeded.

T1566.name: Phishing
T1566.guidance: Malicious messages or attachments. Rarely visible in network flow data alone; a flow-based match to phishing is weak evidence and usually warrants human review.

T1190.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
T1190.guidance: Attacks against internet-facing services (e.g. web attacks, SQL injection, XSS, or Heartbleed against a TLS service). Blocking the source and isolating or patching the targeted service is appropriate. Escalate if the service holds sensitive data.

T1041.name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
T1041.guidance: Data leaving through an existing command-and-control channel (e.g. botnet traffic). Isolating the internal host is appropriate; the host is likely compromised, so escalation for forensics is usually warranted.

T1567.name: Exfiltration Over Web Service
T1567.guidance: Data sent to a legitimate external web service. Blocking the destination is appropriate, but false positives are common with normal cloud usage; escalate when confidence is not high.

T1498.name: Network Denial of Service
T1498.guidance: Volumetric flooding of a network or service (e.g. DDoS). Rate-limiting or blocking the sources upstream is appropriate. Many sources at once suggest DDoS rather than a single attacker.

T1499.name: Endpoint Denial of Service
T1499.guidance: Exhausting a specific service's resources (e.g. DoS Hulk, GoldenEye, Slowloris, SlowHTTPTest). Blocking or rate-limiting the source is appropriate.

T1046.name: Network Service Discovery
T1046.guidance: Scanning for open ports and services (e.g. PortScan). Usually reconnaissance before an attack: blocking the scanning source is low-risk and appropriate.
